Only the current HFM files are used; the Deprecated subdirectory is excluded, as in the primary nonrecursive reduction. Stock-thickness metadata identifies the population and does not prescribe geometry or replace actual HFM thicknesses. Capacity and conductivity are different experiments on the same product/conditioning population, without proof of the exact same physical coupon. No strength, expansion, phase-change, optical, fire-performance or service-temperature qualification is supplied.

Wet in raw filenames denotes unconditioned indoor storage at 22 +/- 3 degC and relative humidity 40 +/- 20 percent, not water saturation or oven drying. General HFM preparation makes planar samples. Conductivity is through thickness with upward heat flow, generally following ASTM C518; capacity follows the general ASTM C1784-20 equal-plate temperature-step method. Material-axis mapping, applied contact pressure, calibration uncertainty and cross-property covariance are unavailable. Three conductivity cycles on one specimen do not constitute three independent specimens.

Following the primary script, round mean temperatures to 0.1 degC, grouping these rows at 10,20,30,40 degC. Mean C_vol is the arithmetic mean of three native values; add exactly 273.15 for kelvin. Separate sample SD is sqrt(sum((C_i-mean_C)^2)/(3-1)); it is TabulatedOnly, not a confidence interval or calibration uncertainty. Extra computed digits represent arithmetic, not improved measurement resolution. Linear C_vol(T) and published Cp(T) interpolation is an authored approximation between groups, without an interpolation error bound or extrapolation. Native C_vol requires no density(T).

The files Nylon_Density_Wet_R1.csv, Nylon_Density_Wet_R2.csv and Nylon_Density_Wet_R3.csv report density columns 1065,1074,1072 kg/m3, masses 146.40000000000001,145.69999999999999,146.80000000000001 g and volumes 137.40000000000001,135.59999999999999,136.90000000000001 cm3. The reduction uses the mean of those reported rounded density entries, 1070.3333333333333 kg/m3, rather than recomputing mass/volume or substituting the metadata headline 1070 kg/m3. Density measurement temperature is unreported. This reference-normalization input has no temperature validity and is not a continuous bulk-density law.

FSRI divides the mean native C_vol by the condition-mean reported density, then rounds to whole J/(kg K), giving 1519,1623,1755,1836 at 10,20,30,40 degC. Published SD is native capacity sample SD divided by that same mean density, rounded to whole units: 24,31,40,39 J/(kg K). Density scatter and calibration covariance are not propagated. C_vol, rounded Cp and normalization density are algebraically related, not independent measurements.
